_comment: WHERE AN ACTOR'S FEET ARE, AND HOW ITS ANIMATIONS ARE TIMED -- authored,
not guessed. Before this file the runtime inferred all three of those
numbers by scanning pixels and applying global constants, and every
inference was eventually wrong about something: the golem's ground slam
erupts an earth spike ~50px BELOW its feet and Shawn's idle plants a staff
~33px below his, so a scan for 'the lowest opaque pixel' read both as the
floor and hoisted the figures off the ground. See docs/ART_PIPELINE.md.
groundLine: pixels from the sprite canvas's BOTTOM EDGE up to the surface
the figure stands on. One value per actor, not per stance, because a
character's feet do not move relative to their own art -- only the effects
drawn around them do. That is what stops a figure jumping between poses.
stances: only poses with MORE THAN ONE FRAME need an entry, since timing
is meaningless for a still. StanceManifestValidationTests fails if a
multi-frame stance is missing one, so this cannot silently fall behind the
art. Single-frame poses take the defaults in StanceManifestResolver.
Lives in Resources/ rather than ContentData/ because it is read at RUNTIME
rather than baked by ContentBuilder, and deliberately NOT under
Resources/Content/, which ContentBuilder deletes wholesale on every run.

actors._groundLineNote: Every forest_warden frame was cropped independently to its own content bounding box plus a uniform 14px pad on every side, rather than sliced off one shared-canvas sheet the way golem/rat were -- so this value is that pad, not a measured foot position. It should hold well for idle/attack/attack_roar/attack_charge, where the feet are consistently each frame's lowest point; hurt and defeated change body orientation enough that a small vertical pop between stances is possible and worth an eyeball pass in the editor.

stances._note: 0.2 rather than the 0.1 every other Warden stance runs at, on request -- the roar reads as the fight's turning point and was over faster than its plain swing. Doubling the pace doubles the beat: FightBeatPlayer budgets a beat at secondsPerFrame x FrameCount, so nothing in code had to change for this.

actors._loopNote: The beetle's idle is authored as a COMPLETE cycle -- measured, not assumed: the step from its last drawing back to its first is 18.9 units of mean pixel difference against a 11.8-20.3 spread across the other five, i.e. unremarkable. So it plays forward. The Treant's and the Warden's are half-cycles whose wrap is the biggest step in the sequence, and both stay on the ping-pong default. See Domain/Stage/LoopCycle.
actors._groundLineNote: Delivered by tools/pad_actor_frames.py, which bottom-aligns every frame -- so unlike forest_warden's, this ground line cannot drift between stances. Impact frames below are eyeballed off the art: the beetle's bite lands as the mandibles open (f2, 1-indexed 3) and the roll connects late (f5).
As above. The slam lands when the trunk is fully over (f3) and the spore burst when the arms reach their widest (f4).
